extracted.intended_audience: HHS awarding agencies, grant administrators, recipients and subrecipients of HHS federal awards (including States and foreign grantees)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and program-specific amendments describing applicability of 2 CFR parts 200 and 300, cost principles, allowability of certain costs, payment/cash management rules, and conditions for revisions to budgets and program plans for HHS grants and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of 2 CFR parts 200 and 300 (Uniform Administrative Requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: 2 CFR parts 200 and 300—Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards apply as 'Other HHS regulations that apply' across numerous HHS program parts and sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeatedly adds in alphanumeric order an entry for '2 CFR parts 200 and 300' and removes references to 45 CFR part 75, indicating that grantees and administering units must follow 2 CFR parts 200 and 300 (including subpart E where noted) in lieu of prior 45 CFR part 75 cross-references. This change is inserted into many program-specific sections to make 2 CFR parts 200 and 300 the controlling uniform administrative requirements for Federal awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal payment governed by CMIA and program income use before additional cash
rubrics_metrics.description: For States, payments are governed by Treasury-State Cash Management Improvement Act (CMIA) agreements and default procedures codified at 31 CFR part 205 and TFM 4A-2000 Overall Disbursing Rules for All Federal Agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To the extent that Treasury-State CMIA agreements and default procedures do not address expenditure of program income, rebates, refunds, contract settlements, audit recoveries and interest earned on such funds, such funds must be expended before requesting additional cash payments. (Applies in addition to 2 CFR 200.305(b).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval required for inclusion of research patient care costs
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient or subrecipient must request approval from the Federal agency or pass-through entity for the inclusion of research patient care costs in research awards made for the performance of research work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is in addition to 2 CFR 200.308(f). Recipients/subrecipients should not include research patient care costs in award budgets or claim reimbursement without prior approval from the awarding agency or pass-through entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intangible property: no agency rights to inventions in primarily educational awards
rubrics_metrics.description: No scholarship, fellowship, training grant, or other funding agreement made primarily to a recipient for educational purposes will contain any provision giving the Federal agency rights to inventions made by the recipient or subrecipient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is in addition to 2 CFR 200.315(c). Educational-purpose awards must not include clauses assigning invention/patent rights to the Federal agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect cost cap for training grants (8% MTDC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs on training grants are limited to a fixed rate of eight percent of MTDC exclusive of tuition and related fees, direct expenditures for equipment, and subawards in excess of $25,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision supplements 2 CFR 200.414(c). Training grant budgets and reimbursements must apply the 8% fixed rate on modified total direct costs (MTDC) after excluding the listed categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs for foreign organizations performing fully outside U.S. (8% MTDC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs on grants awarded to foreign organizations and foreign public entities and performed fully outside of the territorial limits of the U.S. may be paid to support the costs of compliance with federal requirements at a fixed rate of eight percent of MTDC exclusive of tuition and related fees, direct expenditures for equipment, and subawards in excess of $25,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a fixed-rate indirect cost allowance for fully foreign-performed grants, distinct from negotiated U.S. rates, and should be applied in budgeting and reimbursements for eligible foreign awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for negotiated indirect costs for specified international organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Negotiated indirect costs may be paid to the American University, Beirut, and the World Health Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite the fixed-rate rules above, these named institutions may receive negotiated indirect cost rates; awarding officials should apply negotiated agreements as appropriate for those entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent research and development costs are unallowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent research and development is research and development which is conducted by an organization, and which is not sponsored by Federal or non-Federal awards, contracts, or other agreements. The cost of independent research and development, including their proportionate share of indirect costs, are unallowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent R&D must be allocated its proportionate share of indirect costs on the same basis as the allocation of indirect costs to sponsored research and development, but the total cost (including proportionate indirects) is unallowable under HHS Federal awards. See §300.477 for definition and treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shared responsibility payments not allowable costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments or assessments imposed under certain Internal Revenue Code provisions for failures related to health coverage are not allowable expenses under Federal awards from an HHS awarding agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically: (a) Payments under 26 U.S.C. 5000A(b) for failure to maintain minimum essential coverage for periods prior to January 1, 2019, are not allowable; (b) Payments under 26 U.S.C. 4980H imposed on employers for failure to offer minimum essential coverage are not allowable. Such payments must not be charged to HHS federal awards.
